question: Can an existing dataset jointly provide source-grounded natural language, executable strong revision, productive SCC/LFP closure, acquisition pressure, and real provenance?

verdict.recommended_strategy: Keep ProofWriter/ParaRules as the SCC-LFP mechanism block; add a controlled strong-revision block and a real temporal external block.
verdict.plain_language: No single dataset does everything. The strongest paper design is a three-block evidence stack, not a forced replacement of the datasets already audited.

strong_revision_gates.label: Sequential state
strong_revision_gates.definition: The same query has an explicit before and after state.

strong_revision_gates.label: True strong revision
strong_revision_gates.definition: A previously supported answer is invalidated and the opposite or a different dated answer becomes supported.

strong_revision_gates.label: Executable certificate
strong_revision_gates.definition: An independent engine or deterministic scorer can verify the change.

strong_revision_gates.label: Source-grounded NL
strong_revision_gates.definition: The changed evidence is linked to text; human or real provenance is preferred.

strong_revision_gates.label: Productive SCC
strong_revision_gates.definition: A query-relevant recursive component is causal rather than decorative.

strong_revision_gates.label: Acquisition pressure
strong_revision_gates.definition: The decisive source is hidden among distractors and must be selected under budget.

strong_revision_gates.label: Reproducible release
strong_revision_gates.definition: Data, license, version, and reconstruction path are available.

preserved_evidence_stack.kept_for: Executable positive-Horn closure, predicate-SCC contribution, and multi-source acquisition pressure.
Independent fact-acquisition, proof, noise, and closure transfer checks.
Real source spans and citation-linked cyclic evidence; not logical truth gold.

candidates.name: TKGQA (financial M&A)
candidates.strength: The only release found in this wave that jointly exposes real source sentences, event tuples, deterministic before/after graph updates, graph diffs, and aligned QA.
candidates.limit: Questions are templated, extraction quality is imperfect, and the observed entity SCCs are not predicate-SCC proof regions; a high-precision manually audited subset is required.

candidates.name: ReviseQA
candidates.strength: The cleanest executable T↔F revision protocol found in this wave.
candidates.limit: Natural language is model-generated from formal problems; almost none of the strong flips live in strict positive-Horn SCCs.

candidates.name: FiscalQA Pro
candidates.strength: Real French tax-law versions, expert-reviewed questions, exact version provenance, deterministic nuggets, and clear licensing.
candidates.limit: The scored task is usually single-article temporal retrieval; citation SCCs are not executable rule SCCs and there is no old-proof invalidation certificate.

candidates.name: LawShift
candidates.strength: Large controlled legal revision set with a useful fact-fixed, law-changed subset.
candidates.limit: The revisions are expert-designed counterfactuals rather than observed historical amendments; no proof or SCC gold.

candidates.name: MQuAKE-Remastered-T
candidates.strength: Real Wikidata temporal changes with explicit old/new answers and short multi-hop chains.
candidates.limit: The chains are simple DAG paths, most edits hit the last hop, and questions are model-generated.

candidates.name: BoardgameQA
candidates.strength: Exact defeasible priorities make genuine defeat and answer reversal mechanically checkable.
candidates.limit: The 425 cases are construction candidates, not native before/after pairs; grounded cycles are effectively absent.

candidates.name: LogicNLI
candidates.strength: Dense predicate-SCC structure, machine-readable logic, and proof expressions.
candidates.limit: Static paraconsistent contradiction is not revision; the repository has no explicit data license.

candidates.name: MultiLogicNMRer
candidates.strength: Exact ASP semantics, multiple extensions, and extension-level proofs make it a strong nonmonotonic boundary test.
candidates.limit: Most cycles are created by default negation rather than positive-Horn recursion; static only and no repository license.

candidates.name: Belief-R
candidates.strength: Directly studies human-style belief suppression and maintenance.
candidates.limit: No executable proof, SCC, or true T↔F flip; much of the text is GPT-4 generated from ATOMIC.

recommended_paper_stack.name: Mechanism block
recommended_paper_stack.claim: LFP-guided acquisition and state sharing in productive predicate-SCCs.

recommended_paper_stack.name: Controlled strong-revision block
recommended_paper_stack.claim: A later source can invalidate a prior proof and support a different conclusion under executable revision semantics.

recommended_paper_stack.name: Real temporal external block
recommended_paper_stack.claim: The old answer is genuinely obsolete in real versioned knowledge, with exact provenance.

recommended_paper_stack.name: Preserved transfer block
recommended_paper_stack.claim: The acquisition/closure interface transfers beyond the main synthetic rule family.

semantic_guardrail: Within each frozen program snapshot, positive-Horn LFP is monotone. A true T↔F revision across snapshots requires rule/fact removal, supersession, priority, exception, or temporal validity; it must not be described as ordinary monotone LFP growth.
next_actions: Build a high-precision TKGQA subset from the 5,840 aligned answer changes and audit whether asset propagation creates long, query-causal dependency chains.
Run a small ReviseQA branch-safe revision prototype and keep only source-grounded, solver-verified edits.
Freeze the 184 FiscalQA adjacent answer-change pairs and separately inspect the 17 targets in approximate citation SCCs.
Construct matched productive-SCC versus DAG strong-revision controls without changing proof depth, source count, or language style.
Keep the current ProofWriter/ParaRules and P1 experiments unchanged until the revision track independently passes its gates.
